# Paired t-test sample size calculation
# Parameters
mean_diff <- 3  # kg - expected weight reduction
sd_baseline <- 5  # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5  # kg
r <- 0.5  # within-person correlation
alpha <- 0.05  # one-sided test
target_power <- 0.80

# Calculate SD of the difference
# SD_diff = sqrt(SD_baseline^2 + SD_followup^2 - 2*r*SD_baseline*SD_followup)
sd_diff <- sqrt(sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2*r*sd_baseline*sd_followup)
cat("SD of paired differences:", sd_diff, "kg\n")

# Calculate effect size (Cohen's d for paired data)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd_diff
cat("Cohen's d (paired):", cohens_d, "\n")

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha=0.05
# We'll use iterative approach to find n where achieved power = 0.80
# For paired t-test: t_crit = qt(1 - alpha, df = n-1)
# Non-centrality parameter: lambda = d * sqrt(n)
# Power = 1 - pt(t_crit, df=n-1, ncp=lambda)

library(stats)

# Function to calculate power for given sample size (paired t-test)
power_paired_t <- function(n, effect_size, alpha = 0.05, one_sided = TRUE) {
  df <- n - 1
  
  # Critical value (one-sided)
  if (one_sided) {
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)
  } else {
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = df)
  }
  
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- effect_size * sqrt(n)
  
  # Power calculation
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = ncp)
  
  return(power)
}

# Find minimum sample size for target power = 0.80
sample_sizes <- 2:500
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) power_paired_t(n, cohens_d, alpha, one_sided = TRUE))

# Find minimum n where power >= 0.80
min_n <- sample_sizes[which(powers >= target_power)[1]]
achieved_power_min_n <- powers[which(sample_sizes == min_n)[1]]

cat("\n--- Sample Size Calculation ---\n")
cat("Minimum sample size for 80% power:", min_n, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", round(achieved_power_min_n, 4), "\n")

# Also report power at n-1 to show the crossing
if (min_n > 2) {
  prev_n <- min_n - 1
  prev_power <- power_paired_t(prev_n, cohens_d, alpha, one_sided = TRUE)
  cat("Power at n =", prev_n, ":", round(prev_power, 4), "\n")
  cat("Power improvement from n =", prev_n, "to n =", min_n, ":",
      round(achieved_power_min_n - prev_power, 4), "\n")
}

# Display a range for verification
cat("\n--- Power by Sample Size ---\n")
verification_ns <- c(15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50)
for (n in verification_ns) {
  pw <- power_paired_t(n, cohens_d, alpha, one_sided = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("n = %3d: Power = %.4f %s\n", n, pw, if (pw >= 0.80) "[✓ meets target]" else ""))
}

# Emit result
result <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = min_n,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

cat("\n--- Final Result ---\n")
print(result)

cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd_diff_manual
cat("   d = mean_diff / SD_diff\n")
cat("   d = 3 / ", sd_diff_manual, "\n")
cat("   d = ", cohens_d, "\n\n")

# Parameters
mean_diff <- 3  # kg - expected weight reduction
sd_baseline <- 5  # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5  # kg
r <- 0.5  # within-person correlation
alpha <- 0.05  # one-sided test
target_power <- 0.80

# Calculate SD of the difference
# SD_diff = sqrt(SD_baseline^2 + SD_followup^2 - 2*r*SD_baseline*SD_followup)
sd_diff <- sqrt(sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2*r*sd_baseline*sd_followup)
cat("SD of paired differences:", sd_diff, "kg\n")

# Calculate effect size (Cohen's d for paired data)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd_diff
cat("Cohen's d (paired):", cohens_d, "\n")

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha=0.05
# We'll use iterative approach to find n where achieved power = 0.80
# For paired t-test: t_crit = qt(1 - alpha, df = n-1)
# Non-centrality parameter: lambda = d * sqrt(n)
# Power = 1 - pt(t_crit, df=n-1, ncp=lambda)

library(stats)

# Function to calculate power for given sample size (paired t-test)
power_paired_t <- function(n, effect_size, alpha = 0.05, one_sided = TRUE) {
  df <- n - 1
  
  # Critical value (one-sided)
  if (one_sided) {
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)
  } else {
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = df)
  }
  
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- effect_size * sqrt(n)
  
  # Power calculation
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = ncp)
  
  return(power)
}

# Find minimum sample size for target power = 0.80
sample_sizes <- 2:500
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) power_paired_t(n, cohens_d, alpha, one_sided = TRUE))

# Find minimum n where power >= 0.80
min_n <- sample_sizes[which(powers >= target_power)[1]]
achieved_power_min_n <- powers[which(sample_sizes == min_n)[1]]

cat("\n--- Sample Size Calculation ---\n")
cat("Minimum sample size for 80% power:", min_n, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", round(achieved_power_min_n, 4), "\n")

# Also report power at n-1 to show the crossing
if (min_n > 2) {
  prev_n <- min_n - 1
  prev_power <- power_paired_t(prev_n, cohens_d, alpha, one_sided = TRUE)
  cat("Power at n =", prev_n, ":", round(prev_power, 4), "\n")
  cat("Power improvement from n =", prev_n, "to n =", min_n, ":",

}

# Emit result

  metric = "sample_size",
  value = min_n,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha=0.05
# We'll use iterative approach to find n where achieved power = 0.80
# For paired t-test: t_crit = qt(1 - alpha, df = n-1)
# Non-centrality parameter: lambda = d * sqrt(n)
# Power = 1 - pt(t_crit, df=n-1, ncp=lambda)

library(stats)

# Function to calculate power for given sample size (paired t-test)
power_paired_t <- function(n, effect_size, alpha = 0.05, one_sided = TRUE) {
  df <- n - 1
  
  # Critical value (one-sided)
  if (one_sided) {
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)
  } else {
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = df)
  }
  
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- effect_size * sqrt(n)
  
  # Power calculation
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = ncp)
  
  return(power)
}
